content.text: {"deal_state_line":"Waiting on customer: Ben deferred next steps with no date ('We'll be in touch'), Helen has unresolved capacity and migration worries, and CFO Farah has not been engaged.","customer_value_line":"Ben's stated outcome: store managers know by mid afternoon what to reorder instead of finding out from an empty shelf the next morning; the demo showed ship from store orders merged with store sales, updated every five minutes.","what_we_validated":["Store sales and ship from store orders merged in one model, updated every five minutes (sample SKU: on hand twelve, nine ship from store orders, real number three)","SKU matching via the customer's crosswalk table: about four percent of rows unmatched, listed in an exceptions table; Raymond said four percent is better than today","Replenishment projection per store and SKU against the reorder point","Alerts by email and Teams; Raymond said Teams is what store managers use; alerts can route to district managers via the district field","Sized for about 640 stores per Tom; the sandbox used twenty stores"],"integration_patterns":["Connectors for the POS system and the ecommerce database, with models built with Apex help in the first weeks; customer owns the SKU crosswalk","POS extracts unchanged; Apex reads the files where they land today","Teams alerts to store managers, routable to district managers","Backfill about two years of POS history in the current format; touch the old format only if the model needs it"],"objections_and_answers":["Helen, implementation effort and capacity ('timing', 'a lot on our plate', last migration took four months and she lost two engineers): Tom said Apex would build connectors and first models with her team and crosswalk ownership stays with the customer, but gave no timeline or effort estimate. Status: open","Ben, why Apex over Lakestream (marketing uses it; boss will ask, 'one vendor instead of two'): Tom said the five minute inventory merge is a streaming problem and Lakestream needs a separate streaming product; Elise suggested comparing on the actual workload; Raymond said marketing loads daily; Ben said he'll take it back. Status: partially resolved","Ben, pricing: Elise said it is based on compute and number of connected sources, not per store or per user, and she will put together a range after Tom looks at the full store count. Status: open","Raymond, seasonality: sandbox only extrapolates from one week; in production backfill at least a year with same week last year as an input; Tom would not promise peak performance before seeing the customer's history. Status: open"],"open_items":["Realistic implementation plan with customer effort by role and no guessed timeline (owner: Tom, no date stated)","Seasonality and peak behavior on the customer's history (owner: Tom, no date stated)","Review of the SKU exceptions table, mostly discontinued items (owner: Raymond)","Raymond wants to see a Teams alert set up for a real store, not urgent (owner: Tom, no date stated)","Pricing range sized on the full store count (owner: Elise, no date stated)","Customer owner for the SKU crosswalk not named","No dated next meeting agreed;
